investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Available Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-17T00:52–01:00Z because every pod submitted to the Kubernetes cluster was rejected as Unschedulable: 2 of 6 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No preemption path was available, so the pods remained stuck for ~144–146 seconds before the eval timed out and returned empty evidence.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted the allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry that resource type. The other 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector, leaving zero schedulable nodes for any new remote-agent pod. Because no pod could be scheduled, the createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs never completed, and the eval returned no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState all missing), causing the contract validation to fail. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.' — the scheduler message names the exact resource constraint and node count.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=150464, status=fail — the pod was stuck for 146s before the eval gave up, consistent with a scheduling deadlock rather than a transient API error.
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical Unschedulable message (144s stuck), same node breakdown (2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 affinity mismatch).
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical Unschedulable message (145s stuck), same node breakdown.

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required evidence keys (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent — consistent with the probe never reaching the agent-creation step because the pod never started.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1884-1885: the runner calls requireOrgId then createAgent with machineType='remote'; if the remote pod cannot be scheduled, createAgent never returns and no evidence is written.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:256-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState in [running, idle, ready]; neither assertion can be evaluated because the evidence object is empty.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots on the peer-pod-capable nodes are occupied by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector rules, which may indicate a label was removed, a node pool was replaced, or the pod spec targets a node group that no longer exists at sufficient scale.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning: the total number of kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes (2) may be insufficient for the concurrent load of eval probes plus production workloads, with no headroom for new scheduling.

Lower probability — transient spike in remote-agent demand consuming all VM slots just before the eval window: if existing agents were not cleaned up promptly, slots could be temporarily exhausted even if capacity is nominally sufficient.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place new pods: 2 of 6 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No preemption victims were available, so the pods remained unscheduled for ~144–146 seconds before the eval timed out, leaving all required evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) uncollected.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 nodes that are eligible by node affinity. The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector constraints. Because no preemption victims exist on the eligible nodes, the scheduler cannot place the agent pod at all. The eval probe calls createAgent(..., "remote", ...) in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1905), which depends on this pod being scheduled and reaching a ready state before evidence can be collected. Since the pod never schedules, the probe exits with the scheduler error message and returns no evidence, causing the contract validation to fail on all four required fields: orgId, agentId, readyState, and state. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agents VM pool; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

The other 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity or selector. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on the 2 eligible nodes. This is a cluster-level resource exhaustion condition localized to the remote-agent VM pool, not an application code defect. This is an eval-detected infrastructure condition; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence to confirm a user-facing outage.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Available Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-17T00:52–01:00Z because every pod submitted to the Kubernetes cluster was rejected as Unschedulable: 2 of 6 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No preemption path was available, so the pods remained stuck for ~144–146 seconds before the eval timed out and returned empty evidence.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted the allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry that resource type. The other 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector, leaving zero schedulable nodes for any new remote-agent pod. Because no pod could be scheduled, the createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs never completed, and the eval returned no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState all missing), causing the contract validation to fail. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.' — the scheduler message names the exact resource constraint and node count.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=150464, status=fail — the pod was stuck for 146s before the eval gave up, consistent with a scheduling deadlock rather than a transient API error.
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical Unschedulable message (144s stuck), same node breakdown (2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 affinity mismatch).
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical Unschedulable message (145s stuck), same node breakdown.

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required evidence keys (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent — consistent with the probe never reaching the agent-creation step because the pod never started.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1884-1885: the runner calls requireOrgId then createAgent with machineType='remote'; if the remote pod cannot be scheduled, createAgent never returns and no evidence is written.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:256-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState in [running, idle, ready]; neither assertion can be evaluated because the evidence object is empty.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots on the peer-pod-capable nodes are occupied by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector rules, which may indicate a label was removed, a node pool was replaced, or the pod spec targets a node group that no longer exists at sufficient scale.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning: the total number of kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes (2) may be insufficient for the concurrent load of eval probes plus production workloads, with no headroom for new scheduling.

Lower probability — transient spike in remote-agent demand consuming all VM slots just before the eval window: if existing agents were not cleaned up promptly, slots could be temporarily exhausted even if capacity is nominally sufficient.
